meta.title: The Broad Street Vault Breach: Sub-Level Infiltration
meta.incidentLocation: First Federal Depository, Sub-Level 2 Vault, 140 Broad Street
meta.category: Commercial Burglary, Cyber Intrusion & Aggravated Assault
meta.prosecutor: ADA Eleanor Vance-Wright, Financial Crimes & Special Prosecutions
meta.medicalExaminer: Dr. Rebecca Lin, MD, FCAP (Forensic Clinical Director)
meta.summary: Perpetrators breached Sub-Level 2 reinforced steel vault using an exothermic thermite cutting lance and replay attack against RFID badge readers. Night security officer Mateo Cruz was assaulted and zip-tied. High-value safe deposit boxes exfiltrated. Physical trace recovered copper-aluminum slag and suspect blood droplets on breached hinge plate.

timeline.title: Sub-Level Access Terminal Credential Replay
timeline.description: RFID badge ID #CRUZ-9012 duplicated and replayed via spoofed software handshake.

timeline.title: Physical Assault on Night Guard
timeline.description: Officer Mateo Cruz attacked from behind with blunt instrument; secured with nylon zip-ties.

timeline.title: Exothermic Thermal Lance Activation
timeline.description: Extreme localized temperature spike (>2,400°C) recorded on vault door upper hinge.

timeline.title: Perimeter Van Departure
timeline.description: Charcoal commercial van observed speeding northbound with obscured license plates.

intake.name: Officer Mateo Cruz
intake.receivingTechnician: Dr. Alan Mercer, MD (Forensic Clinical Examiner)

belongingsInventory.description: Duty belt with sidearm missing and empty radio pouch
Binding recovered from victim wrists showing tensile fracture

initialTriageVitals.pupils: Equal, round, reactive to light (3.5 mm bilateral)

intake.clinicalNotes: Living victim presented following physical restraint during commercial burglary. Conscious, oriented x4. Presents with 4.5 cm scalp laceration along left occiput and superficial 1st-degree thermal flash burns across right cervical and facial skin.

vaccines.evidentiaryRelevance: Protective coverage against wound contamination from metal vault fragments.

diagnosticTests.clinicalInterpretation: Confirms officer was entirely unimpaired during duty shift.
Consistent with acute inhalation of combustion gases from exothermic lance operation.

traumaPoints.label: Occipital Scalp Laceration
traumaPoints.finding: Linear 4.2 cm laceration with contused margins along left occipital bone without depressed skull fracture.
traumaPoints.evidentiaryValue: Inflicted with cylindrical metallic rod; weapon dimension matches tactical pry bar.

traumaPoints.label: Bilateral Wrist Constriction Markings
traumaPoints.finding: Circumferential erythematous furrowing with petechiae along flexor creases of both wrists.
traumaPoints.evidentiaryValue: Corresponds to 3.6 mm commercial nylon cable tie recovered at scene.

intake.name: Silas Drake

belongingsInventory.description: Sub-GHz and 125kHz RFID emulator loaded with cloned First Federal credentials
Heavy protective gloves encrusted with gray metallic slag particulate

intake.clinicalNotes: Arrestee presents with minor 1.2 cm jagged laceration on right thumb knuckle and small thermal flash burns on anterior forearms.

diagnosticTests.testName: Vault Hinge Blood Droplet Short Tandem Repeat (STR)
diagnosticTests.quantitativeResult: Full Single-Source Profile matching Silas Drake (24/24 Loci, LR 1 in 12 Trillion)
diagnosticTests.clinicalInterpretation: Blood recovered from the cut thermal lance hinge plate conclusively belongs to suspect Silas Drake.

diagnosticTests.testName: Scanning Electron Microscopy / Energy Dispersive X-Ray (SEM-EDS)
diagnosticTests.quantitativeResult: Iron Oxide, Elemental Aluminum, Copper Flakes & Barium Peroxide Slag
diagnosticTests.clinicalInterpretation: Particulate on suspect's hands and gloves is an identical chemical match to thermite lance slag at breached vault.

placards.label: Breached Steel Vault Upper Hinge
placards.description: Severed 4-inch solid carbon steel hinge pin exhibiting thermal liquefaction and solidified copper slag.

placards.label: Dried Blood Droplet on Lower Hinge Lip
placards.description: Two circular passive drip bloodstains (approx 6mm diameter) deposited on jagged cut steel edge.

placards.label: Sub-Level Security Kiosk Terminal
placards.description: RFID access reader with USB interface cable plugged into hidden software relay bug.

placards.label: Discharged Fire Extinguisher Residue
placards.description: Monoammonium phosphate powder coating floor with partial boot print impressions.

evidence.title: Thermite Cutting Lance Slag & Copper Wire Core
evidence.description: Solidified metallic slag containing iron, copper, and aluminum oxide residues.

evidence.title: Hinge Bloodstain Swab (DNA Sample)
evidence.description: Sterile cotton swab of dried blood on severed vault hinge pin.

citizens.alibiClaim: Claims was performing overnight pipe welding at shipyard 15 miles south.

dialogueExchanges.speaker: Detective
dialogueExchanges.text: Mr. Drake, how did your blood end up on the burned hinge pin of Vault Sub-Level 2?

dialogueExchanges.speaker: Suspect
dialogueExchanges.text: I've never been inside First Federal. That's impossible. Your lab made a mistake.

confrontationOptions.title: Confront with Vault Hinge Blood DNA Match
confrontationOptions.contradictionQuote: I've never set foot inside that bank vault.
confrontationOptions.confrontationScript: Your blood was scraped off the jagged thermal cut on the hinge. 24 of 24 STR markers match you at 1 in 12 Trillion.
confrontationOptions.suspectReaction: Suspect glances at right thumb, heart rate climbs to 128 BPM.
confrontationOptions.confessionYield: Admission of handling the thermal lance and cutting hand on the hinge.

exhibits.description: GlobalFiler 24-Plex capillary electrophoresis matching defendant Silas Drake to crime scene.

exhibits.title: SEM-EDS Metallurgy Report: Thermite Slag Comparison
exhibits.description: Identical elemental profile of exothermic cutting lance slag from scene and defendant's gloves.

witnesses.name: Dr. Soren Dahl, PhD
directTestimony: The cutting temperatures exceeded 2,400 degrees Celsius, indicative of specialized thermite composition.
The microscopic slag recovered from the defendant's welding gloves is elementally identical to the breached vault hinge.

crossExaminationQuestions.question: Could standard structural welding produce identical slag?
crossExaminationQuestions.expectedAnswer: No. The presence of barium peroxide oxidizer and micro-copper beads is unique to specialized breaching lances.
